Various Technological Infrastructure and Facilities in Schools 
 
4920. Shri Tatkare Sunil Dattatrey: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number and percentage of schools having the following facilities such as constant electricity 
supply, internet connection, printer, desktop and Children With Special Needs (CWSN) friendly 
washrooms in the country, State/UT-wise; 
(b) the number of schools that have organised at least one medical camp during the last one year in the 
country, State/UT-wise; 
(c) the number and percentage of schools complying with Government prescribed PTR (Pupil Teacher 
Ratio) norms in the country, State/UT-wise and particularly for the State of Maharashtra; 
(d) the number of schools having only one teacher along with the number of students enrolled in such 
schools and the average PTR in these schools in the country, State/UT-wise and particularly for the State 
of Maharashtra; 
(e) the details of initiatives taken by the Government to fill vacancies in aforementioned schools; and 
(f) the number of technology aids (such as digital smartboards, tablets, etc.) provided under Sam agra 
Shiksha Abhiyan to schools along with the cost incurred in this regard, State/UT-wise? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a): As per Unified District Information System for Education Plus (UDISE+) 2024-25, State/UT wise 
number and percentage of schools having electricity facility, internet connection, computer  and 
Children With Special Needs (CWSN) toilets are available at  
https://www.education.gov.in/en/parl_ques. 
 
(b): As per UDISE+ 2024 -25, State/UT wise percentage of schools which conducted at least one  
medical checkup in last academic year are available at  https://www.education.gov.in/en/parl_ques. 
 
(c): National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 recommends a pupil-teacher ratio (PTR) of under 30:1 at

disadvantaged students.  As per UDISE+ 2024 -25, State/UT wise (including Maharashtra) Pupil 
Teacher Ratio (PTR) is available at  https://www.education.gov.in/en/parl_ques.  
 
(d): As per UDISE+ 2024 -25, State/UT wise (including Maharashtra) single teacher schools and 
enrolment in these schools is available at  https://www.education.gov.in/en/parl_ques. 
 
(e): Education being a subject in the Concurrent List of th e Constitution, an overwhelming majority of 
the schools in the country comes under the administrative control of States/UTs. The recruitment, service 

conditions and rational deployment of teachers fall under the purview of the respective State 
Governments/UT Administrations. Recruitment of teachers is a continuous process, and vacancies arise 
on account of various factors such as retirement, resignation and increased requirement of teachers due 
to growth in student enrolment. The Central Government through the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of 
Samagra Shiksha, provides financial assistance to the States and UTs to maintain appropriate Pupil -
Teacher Ratio (PTR) for various levels of schooling, as per norms prescribed in the Right of Children to 
Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, as amended from time to time. 
(f): Under Samagra Shiksha, State/UT wise  physical and financial sanctions of ICT and smart 
classrooms for the year 2025 -26 and tablets for elementary level teachers for the same period  are 
available at  https://www.education.gov.in/en/parl_ques.

“Suspension of New Investments in the Motilal Oswal Nifty Micro-cap 250 Index Fund” 
 
QUESTION 
 
4921. Shri Jagannath Sarkar 
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has suspended new 
investments into the Motilal Oswal Nifty Micro -cap 250 Index Fund from 8 January, 2026 
due to the absence of a recognised "micro -cap" category under the current mutual fund

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION 4923 
ANSWERED ON 23.03.2026 
 
STATUS OF ITIs AND NSTIs IN TELANGANA 
 
4923. DR. KADIYAM KAVYA   
 
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP  be pleased to 
state? 
 
(a)  the number of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and National Skill Training Institutes  
(NSTIs) functioning in Telangana, including in Warangal Lok Sabha Constituency, along with the  
number of trades offered and trainees enrolled during the last three years and the current year,  
district-wise; 
 
(b)  the steps taken/being taken by the Government to modernize infrastructure, update curricula 
and align ITI/NSTI courses with emerging technologies, such as Artificial Intelligence,  Internet of 
Things, Renewable Energy and 3D Printing, particularly in the institutions located in  the said 
Constituency; 
 
(c)  whether the Government has entered into partnerships with industry, including Autodesk  
Inc., for curriculum modernization and trainer upskilling in Telangana and if so, the details thereof; 
and 
 
(d)  the placement rates and apprenticeship linkages achieved in Telangana, district -wise and 
whether any proposal exists to establish new ITIs/NSTIs or Centres of Excellence in Warangal  
along with the timeline for the same? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a)        The Directorate General of Training (DGT), under the Ministry of Skill Development and 
Entrepreneurship (MSDE), implements the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) through a network 
of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) for skilling the youth.  Under CTS, training is imparted in 169 
courses through 14,688 ITIs (Government - 3,345 & Private - 11,343) across the country.  
 
In the State of Telangana, training under the CTS is imparted through 301 ITIs, comprising 69 
Government ITIs and 232 Private ITIs. In the Warangal Lok Sabha Constituency, 30 ITIs are 
functioning, including 03 Government ITIs and 27 Private ITIs. 
 
During the last three years, i.e., from 2022-23 to 2024-25, and the current session 2025-26, under 
CTS, a total of 1,30,094 trainees have been enrolled in Telangana State, including 11,754 trainees 
in the Warangal Lok Sabha Constituency. 
 
The district-wise number of ITIs, the number of CTS trades offered, and enrolment in ITIs during 
the last three years, i.e., from 2022-23 to 2024-25, and the current session 2025-26, is available at 
Annexure-1. 
 
National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs) impart training under the Craft Instructor Training Scheme 
(CITS) with the objective of equipping instructor trainees with comprehensive hands -on skills and 
training methodology, thereby enabling them to effectively train skilled manpower for industry. 
 

In the State of Telangana, three NSTIs are functioning, all located in Hyderabad district, namely 
NSTI (Women) Hyderabad, NSTI -Ramanthapur and NSTI -Vidyanagar. Under CITS, 17 courses 
are being conducted across these three NSTIs in Telangana. During the period from 2022 -23 to 
2025-26, 1,687 trainees have been enrolled in these NSTIs. 
 
(b)        The trade curriculum is updated periodically in consultation with industry, academia, and 
State/UT Governments to integrate emerging technologies, modern tools & equipment, and 
machinery. In addition, the DGT has introduced 31 New Age trades covering emerging areas such 
as Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things, Renewable Energy and 3D Printing . The List of these 
New Age Trades is placed at Annexure-2. In Warangal Lok Sabha Constituency, 07 New Age 
trades are currently being offered in 04 ITIs. 
 
Further, the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) Scheme 
is launched to enhance the overall quality and relevance of vocational training with upgraded labs, 
machines, and industry -aligned curriculum in the country. The scheme includes upgradation of 
1,000 Government ITIs (200 Hub ITIs and 800 Spoke ITIs) in a Hub and Spoke model wherein 
upgradation includes smart classrooms, modern labs, digital content, and new courses aligned to 
industry needs through industry-led Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs). The selection of ITIs under 
the PM-SETU Scheme is led by the respective State/UT Governments in consultation with industry, 
ensuring alignment with emerging skill needs and local industrial potential. 
 
(c)        The DGT has partnered with various industries, including Autodesk India Pvt. Ltd., to 
deliver training in new -age technical and professional skills through self -paced and mentor -led 
courses for trainees of ITIs and NSTIs across the country. 
 
The partnership with Autodesk India focuses on curriculum enhancement and strengthening 
instructional capacity through faculty development programmes for trainers, enabling adoption of 
modern tools and digital workflows relevant to sectors such as manufacturing, design, architectural 
engineering and related areas. In this regard, Faculty Development Programmes are being 
conducted for trainers across the country, including Telangana. 
 
(d)       The district -wise number of  ITI passout candidates engaged as  apprentices under the 
Apprenticeship Training during the last three years, i.e., from 2022-23 to 2024-25, and the current 
session 2025-26, is available at Annexure-3. 
 
The establishment of Government ITIs falls within the jurisdiction of the respective State 
Governments and UT Administrations. Proposals received in this regard are examined and 
processed in accordance with the procedures and timelines prescribed under the affiliation norms. 
As on date, there is no proposal to establish a new ITI/NSTI in the Warangal constituency.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO - 4924 
ANSWERED ON – 23/03/2026 
  
IMPLEMENTATION OF PMKVY IN DHARMAPURI 
  
4924.  SHRI MANI A:  
             
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to 
state:- 
  
(a)       whether the Government has mapped the skill demand and supply gap in Tamil Nadu 
under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) and the extent to which training 
centres in the State are aligned with emerging sectors, such as electronics, re newable energy, 
logistics and healthcare;  
  
(b)       the details of training centres, sanctioned job roles, batch utilisation rates and drop -out 
percentages in Tamil Nadu, district-wise, particularly for Dharmapuri district;  
  
(c)       the percentage of certified candidates in the said district who secured employment within 
six months of certification, along with the details of migration outside the district for jobs;  
  
(d)      whether the wage levels of placed candidates in Dharmapuri district meet minimum wage 
standards and provide sustainable livelihoods and if so, the details thereof; and  
  
(e)      whether the Government proposes to introduce industry-linked apprenticeship clusters or 
women-focused residential skill hubs in Dharmapuri district to improve placement outcomes and 
retention rates and if so, the details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
  
(a)      Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) is implementing Pradhan 
Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana, since 2015, for imparting skill development training through Short-
Term Training (STT) and up-skilling and re-skilling through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) 
to the youth across the country including Tamil Nadu. PMKVY 4.0, which is being implemented 
since 2022, is a demand -driven scheme aimed at bridging skill gaps identified across various 
sectors. The identification of such gaps is facilitated through skill gap studies conducted by the 
Sector Skill Councils. Further, District Skill Committees constituted across all States/UTs 
prepare District Skill Development Plans (DSDPs) to promote decentralized planning for skill 
development and effective implementation at the grassroots level. All 38 districts of Tamil Nadu 
prepared their District Skill Development Plans (DSDPs) for the financial year 2024 –25. These 
plans identify priority sectors with employment potential and assess the corresponding ski lling 
demand. Further, training is aligned with industry requirements through Qualification Packs and 
National Occupational Standards developed in consultation with Awarding Bodies and industry 
stakeholders.  
 
The sector wise detail of candidates trained under PMKVY since inception upto 31.12.2025, 
including emerging sectors such as electronics, renewable energy, logistics and healthcare 
sector, in the State of Tamil Nadu, are given at Annexure I. 

(b)       The district wise details of training centres and drop-out percentages in Tamil Nadu under 
PMKVY since, 2015 to 31.12.2025 is given at Annexure II.  The district wise details of job role 
offered under PMKVY since 2015 to 31.12.2025 is given at Annexure III. Since the details in 
aforementioned Annexure –III is too lengthy, it is uploaded on Ministry’s website 
at https://www.msde.gov.in/documents?page=1.   
 
(c) & (d)         Under PMKVY, placements were tracked in the Short -Term Training (STT) 
component in the first three versions of the Scheme - PMKVY 1.0, PMKVY 2.0 and PMKVY 3.0, 
implemented from FY 2015 -16 to FY 2021 -22.   Under PMKVY 1.0 to 3.0, 4,168 candidates 
have been certified under STT component in the Dharmapuri district of Tamil Nadu, out of which, 
44.86 % candidates have been reported placed.  
 
Under PMKVY 4.0, the focus is to empower our trained candidates to choose their varied career 
path and suitably oriented for the same through industry -relevant skill courses that include On-
the-Job Training (OJT). 
 
An independent third-party impact evaluation of Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 
4.0 conducted by the Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management (AJNIFM) across 
12 States, including Tamil Nadu, has mentioned in its report that PMKVY training has contributed 
to a measurable shift in employment outcomes for STT candidates. The combined share of 
employed and self-employed STT respondents increased from 26.6% prior to training to 45.4% 
after PMKVY training, reflecting an 18.8 percentage point increase. Income -related outcomes 
also show positive movement, with 41.4% of STT candidates and 48.9% of RPL candidates 
reporting an increase in income following training and certification. 
 
(e)     The Government has taken various steps to strengthen industry linkage, increase women 
participation and placement outcomes under PMKVY 4.0. The courses under PMKVY are 
designed by industry-led bodies addressing the requirement of emerging sectors. 
 
Further, to enable the opportunities for employments, Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) platform has 
been launched as a one -stop platform that integrates skilling, education, employment, and 
entrepreneurship ecosystems to provide a lifelong array of services targeting a wide range of 
stakeholders. Details of the trained candidates are available on SIDH portal for connecting with 
potential employers. Through Skill India Digital Hub, candidates can have access to jobs and 
apprenticeship opportunities. Also, On -Job-Training (OJT) has been made an inherent 
component of the PMKVY. Further, Kaushal Mahotsavs and Pradhan Mantri National 
Apprenticeship Melas (PMNAMs) have been organized to facilitate the placements opportunities 
to the certified candidates. 
 
In order to increase the participation of women under PMKVY, conveyance cost and boarding & 
lodging facilities are being provided. PMKVY 4.0 prioritizes and provides special focus to 
projects that emphasize women as primary beneficiaries such as Nurturing Aspirations through 
Vocational Training for Young Adolescent Girls (NAVYA).

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO:- 4925 
ANSWERED ON-23/03/2026 
 
Shortage of Qualified Teachers in Schools 
 
†4925. Smt. Manju Sharma: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether it is a fact that there is a persistent shortage of qualified school teachers in many 
schools in the country, particularly in rural areas of the country; 
(b) if so, the details of the number of schools currently facing this shortage, State-wise; 
(c) whether the Government has taken any specific steps to fill up the vacant posts of school 
teachers, especially in rural areas, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether it is a fact that a large number of vacant posts of teachers  at all levels of primary, 
secondary and higher education in the State of Rajasthan is adversely affecting the teaching 
situation and quality of education and if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the details of steps taken/proposed to be taken by the Govern ment to fill up these vacant 
posts? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
(a) to (e): Education being a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution, the majority of 
schools in the country are under the administrative control of the respective State Governments 
and Union Territory Administrations. Accordingly, matters relating to recr uitment, service 
conditions and deployment of teachers fall within the administrative domain of the concerned 
States/UTs. Vacancies of teachers arise from time to time due to factors such as retirement, 
resignation, creation of new posts, rationalisation a nd increased enrolment, including in rural 
and remote areas. The data regarding vacant posts of teachers and the number of schools facing 
a shortage of teachers , including in the State of Rajasthan, is maintained by the respective 
States/UTs. 
As per the UDISE+ 2024 -25 report, the State/UT -wise details of teachers in position in 
Government schools across the country, including in the State of Rajasthan, are placed in the 
Annexure, available at https://www.education.gov.in/parl_ques.  
The Central Government periodically advises States/UTs to fill vacant posts through 
transparent and merit -based recruitment processes, including through autonomous teacher 
recruitment boards or similar mechanisms. The progr ess of recruitment is regularly reviewed 

through meetings and advisories, with emphasis on competitive selection, consistency and 
technology-based teacher requirement planning and forecasting. 
Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Samagra Shiksha, States /UTs are supported in 
undertaking rational and transparent deployment of teachers, including through online systems, 
to ensure equitable availability of teachers in rural and underserved areas. States/UTs are also 
encouraged to adopt school complex/cluster -based approaches and teacher -sharing 
mechanisms to address localised shortages. 
In order to ensure quality of teachers, the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE), 
vide Gazette notification dated 23rd August, 2010, as amended from time to time, has  laid 
down minimum qualifications for appointment of teachers. 
Further, the Central Government provides financial assistance to States/UTs under Samagra 
Shiksha to maintain appropriate Pupil -Teacher Ratio (PTR) at various levels of schooling in 
accordance with the norms prescribed under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory 
Education (RTE) Act, 2009. 
Para 2.3 of the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 emphasises maintaining a PTR of under 
30:1 in each school and under 25:1 in areas with a high prop ortion of socio -economically 
disadvantaged students. As per UDISE+ data, the PTR at the national level has improved from 
27:1 in 2022-23 to 10 at the Foundational stage, 13 at the Preparatory stage, 14 at the Middle 
stage, and 21 at the Secondary stage in 2024-25. Further, the PTR in Rajasthan stands at 9 at 
the Foundational stage, 11 at the Preparatory stage, 12 at the Middle stage, and 16 at the 
Secondary stage, which is within the norms envisaged under NEP 2020.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4926 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 23.03.2026 
 
Restoration of Major Rivers in Chhattisgarh 
4926. SHRI BRIJMOHAN AGRAWAL:  
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE  be pleased 
to state: 
(a) the status of the restoration of major rivers viz. Mahanadi, Shivnath and Kharun, etc.; 
(b) a detailed roadmap to ensure that these projects do not face further delays, keeping 
in view the critical pollution levels in rivers, like the Kharun; 
(c) the details of measures taken by the Government to prevent the discharge of sewage 
water into rivers in the 16 locations where plants are either under construction or still 
in the planning phase; 
(d) the details of current monitoring mechanism to ensure that the treated water meets 
National Green Tribunal (NGT) mandate of biological and chemical standards 
before being released back into the rivers, State/UT-wise; and 
(e) the mechanism adopted by the Government to integrate the NGT’s restoration 
directives with stricter enforcement on industrial units situated along the banks of 
the Arpa, Hasdeo and Kelo rivers etc.? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE 
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (e) 
Mahanadi River flows through Chhattisgarh and Odisha. Kharun river is a tributary of Shivnath 
River, which is a tributary of Mahanadi. Under National Water Quality Monitoring Programme 
(NWMP), CPCB identifies Polluted River Stretches (PRS) based on the level of organic matter 
which is measured in terms of Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) concentration. The PRS are 
classified under Priority Class I to Priority Class V, Priority I being most polluted with BOD 
value of more than 30 mg/l and Priority V being least polluted with BOD ranging between 3 – 6 
mg/l. 
 
The latest report titled “Polluted River Stretches for Restoration of Water Quality” is published 
by CPCB in 2025 based on the water quality data of year 2022 and 2023 and is available on 
CPCB website at https://cpcb.nic.in/reports-3/.  
 
For rejuvenation of Polluted River Stretches (PRS), comprehensive action plans were prepared 
by River Rejuvenation Committee (RRC) constituted by the respective State Government/ UT 
Administration, under the overall supervision and coordination of Principal Secretary, 
Environment of the concerned State/Union Territory for bringing all the polluted river stretches 
identified by CPCB fit for bathing purposes (i.e. BOD ˂ 3 mg/L and FC ˂ 500 MPN/100 mL). 
The progress of implementation of action plans is reviewed by the RRCs at State Level and by 

Central Monitoring Committee (CMC) constituted at Ministry of Jal Shakti at Central Level. 
Details of Online Continuous Effluent Monitoring Systems (OCEMS) installed by industries in 
the state of Chhattisgarh is available at https://rtdms.cpcb.gov.in/data.  
 
To prevent the discharge of sewage water into rivers, as reported by Chhattisgarh Environment 
Conservation Board (CECB), there are 24 STPs operational and 16 STPs under construction. 
Further, it is reported that Faecal Sludge Treatment Plant (FSTP) have been installed in such 
places where STPs are under construction.  Odisha has 12 sewage treatment plants (STPs).  All 
12 STPs are operational and complying with the prescribed standards. In addition, there are 120 
FSTPs in Odisha.  
The steps taken by the Government for prevention and control of water pollution including strict 
monitoring are given below: 
 
 Regulation of industrial Pollution is enforced through various provisions of the Water 
(Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 under Consent mechanism by the 
respective SPCB / PCC.  
 The Central and State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs) / Pollution Control Pollution 
Committees (PCCS) are implementing the provisions of both the Water (Prevention 
and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 and the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 to 
prevent and control pollution of aquatic resources.  
 The Ministry of Environment Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC) has notified 
“Standards for Emission or Discharge of Environmental Pollutants from various 
Industries” under Schedule-I of the Environment Protection Rules, 1986. The industrial 
sectors, for which specific standards are not available, general standards as notified 
under Schedule-VI of the Environment Protection Rules, 1986 are applicable.  
 The Online Continuous Effluent Monitoring Systems (OCEMS) are installed by 17 
categories of industries and Grossly Polluting Industries (GPIs) in the country as per 
directives issued by CPCB. This initiative provides real-time information on effluent 
quality, enabling the identification of non-complying units and the implementation of 
corrective actions. 
 SPCBs / PCCs have been directed under Section 18(1) (b) of the Water (Prevention & 
Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 to direct concerned agencies in the State/UT to develop 
infrastructure for sewage treatment.    
 CPCB is periodically issuing directions to all the concerned departments in the States 
for management of sewage and waste water in accordance with the provisions of the 
Environment (Protection) Rules, 1986.  For ensuring proper operation of existing STPs, 
Common Effluent Treatment Plants (CETPs) and industrial pollution control, 
directions are also issued under Section 18 (1) (b) of the Water (Prevention and Control 
of Pollution) Act, 1974 as well as under Section 5 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 
1986.  
 CPCB has prepared guidelines for conservation and Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) in 
feasible industrial sectors, along with guidelines for the utilization of treated effluent 
in irrigation. Treated wastewater can be reused in various industrial sectors to reduce 
dependency on freshwater, which enhances sustainability, and promotes effective 
water resource management.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4927 
ANSWERED ON 23.03.2026 
 
Establishment of New Central Educational Institutions 
 
†4927. Shri Devesh Shakya: 
   Shri Babu Singh Kushwaha: 
   Shri Neeraj Maurya: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government proposes to establish new Central educational institutions or        
vocational/skill-based colleges for the benefit of the youth of agriculture -dominated areas 
such as Etah, Kasganj, Jaunpur, Badaun and Bareilly districts and Aonla in Uttar Pradesh, if 
so, the details thereof; 
(b) the amount of funds sanctioned and utilised for the development of laboratories and digital 
infrastructure in Government colleges in the districts of Etah, Kasganj, Jaunpur, Badaun and 
Bareilly under the Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM -USHA) during the last 
three years; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to provide financial assistance or special grants fo r     
introducing special courses in local colleges in Jaunpur, Etah, Kasganj and Aonla region to     
promote agri-entrepreneurship, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) whether the Government has established any special monitoring mechanism or support  
system to address  the difficulties faced by rural students while availing educational loans,  
especially in the district of Etah, Kasganj and Jaunpur, if so, the details thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(Dr. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to ( c): In the State of  Uttar Pradesh, there are 15  centrally funded institutions  including 
Aligarh Muslim University (AMU), Aligarh , University of Allahabad, Prayagraj , Indian Institute 
of Technology (IIT) Kanpur, Indian Institute of Technology, Varanasi (BHU), Indian Institute of 
Management (IIM) Lucknow , Motilal Nehru National Institute of Technology (MNNIT)  
Prayagraj, Indian Institute of Information Technology (IIIT) Allahabad, etc.  

The government  has launched the third phase of Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Ab hiyan 
(RUSA) in June 2023 in the form of Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM -USHA), 
with an outlay of Rs. 12,926.10 crore, including the committed liabilities of the earlier phases 
of RUSA, to cater to the needs of educationally unserved/ underser ved areas. PM-USHA is a 
Centrally Sponsored Scheme aimed at funding specific State government universities and 
colleges, so as to improve their quality by ensuring their conformity to prescribed norms and 
standards.  
In the State of Uttar Pradesh, under various components of the scheme, a total of 204 units , 
for an amount of Rs. 1942.27 Cr (Out of this, central share of Rs. 1173.06 Cr ) have been 
approved including 17 projects amounting to Rs. 217.64 Cr under components New Model 
Degree Colleges, Multi-Disciplinary Education and Research Universities (MERU) , Grants to 
Strengthen Universities (GSU) and Grants to Strengthen Colleges (GSC) in the district of Etah, 
Kasganj, Jaunpur, Badaun and Bareilly . Furthermore, under various components of the 
scheme, States/ UTs may undertake several activities such as (i) setting up start-up incubation 
centres and technology development centres for skill-based courses with the help of Industries/ 
Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME); (ii) MoUs signed with industry  for internship/ 
research/ entrepreneurship/ employment; (iii) placement/ training and certification 
programmes, structural reforms according to the increased industry -ready courses and 
industry-academia linkages; (iv) internship/ apprenticeship embedded degree programme; (v) 
vocational courses for 21st-century skills, internships/ training regarding vocational education; 
(vi) focus on skilling and vocationalization training/ workshops/ placement for females, 
transgenders: (vii) establishing equivalence and  mobility to the students through National 
Credit Framework (NCrF) ; (viii) National Higher Education Qualification Framework ; (ix) 
Academic Bank of Credit (ABC), multiple entry/exit; (x) offering of courses and books / course 
materials in Indian Languages etc. 
(d): To address the difficulties faced by rural students while availing educational loans , a  
dedicated online platform, the PM Vidyalaxmi  portal https://pmvidyalaxmi.co.in has been 
developed on which students, including students from rural area can apply for the education 
loan as well as interest subvention, through a simplified application process to be used by all 
banks. This portal has started operating from 25th February 2025. Loans are made accessible 
through a simple, transparent, student -friendly and entirely digital application process, with a 
simple 2-page application format from a longer 7–8 page format used earlier. A 24X7 toll-free 
helpline 1800 1031 for PMVL portal applications is operational to help the students, HEIs and 
Banks in different stages of application process. More than 25,000 education loans have been 
sanctioned to students of Uttar Pradesh through the PM-Vidyalaxmi portal in the year 2025-26 
(till Feb 2026).

UNSPENT CSR FUNDS  
 
 QUESTION 
†4928. Shri Rajkumar Roat: 
Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the total amount deposited in Government notified funds out of 
unspent Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funds under the Companies Act, 2013 
from the year 2014-15 till date, year-wise; 
(b) whether it is a fact that many companies have not been able to spend the two per 
cent CSR amount; and 
(c) if so, the details and number of such companies, year-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS   AND MINISTER OF 
STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
[SHRI HARSH MALHOTRA] 
(a): The amount transferred by the companies to the funds specified in Schedule VII of 
the Companies Act, 2013 (‘Act’) from the Financial Year 2014 -15 to 2023 -24 is at 
Annexure, which  includes funds transferred from unspent CSR accounts of 
companies. 
 
(b) & (c): As per provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, every company having net 
worth of Rs. 500 crore or more or turnover of Rs. 1000 crore or more or net profit of Rs. 
5 crore or more during immediately preceding financial year shall ensure that it spends, 
in every financial year, at least 2% of the average net profits of the company made 
during the three immediately financial years.  
As per section 135 (5) & (6) of the Act, in the case of an ongoing project, the company 
is required to transfer the unspent amount  to a special account of the company i.e 
‘Unspent CSR Account’, within 30 days from the end of concerned financial year and 
spend the same in pursuance  of its CSR policy within the next three financial years 
from the date of such transfer. After the lapse of three financial years, the amount 
remaining unspent, if any, is required to be transferred to any Fund mentioned in 
Schedule VII of the Act within a period of thirty days from the date of completion of the 
third financial year. In case of other than an ongoing project, the company is required 
to transfer the unspent CSR amount to any Fund mentioned in Schedule VII of the Act 
within a period of six months from the end of concerned financial year.  The Ministry 
does not maintain the details of unspent CSR funds centrally.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

DEPARTMENT OF FINANCIAL SERVICES 
LOK SABHA

 ANSWERED ON MONDAY, MARCH 23, 2026/CHAITRA 02, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
Review of the Reserve Bank of India Act 
 
4929.  SHRI PARSHOTTAMBHAI RUPALA: 
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is examining the need for a comprehensive review and amendment of 
the Reserve Bank of India Act to address the evolving complexities of the Indian economy and 
the current global economic environment, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government has assessed instances of regulatory overlap between the Reserve Bank 
of India and sectoral regulators such as the Securities and Exchange Board of India the Insurance 
Regulatory and Development Authority of India, and the Pension Fund Regulatory and 
Development Authority, if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) whether comparative studies of central bank legislation in countries such as New Zealand and Sri 
Lanka have been undertaken to identify global best practices for possible incorporation into the 
RBI Act, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a) to (c): The amendments to existing Acts are considered, based on assessment of evolving 
landscape, dynamics of the prevailing ecosystem, and to align them with best practices so that the 
Acts remain relevant, effective and able to address the emerging complexities of the economy. 
Further, active and engaging consultations with all the relevant stakeholders are carried out, and best 
practices across other jurisdiction are analyzed, while considering any amendment in existing Acts. It 
was only after extensive deliberations, the provision related to ‘Shifting of submission of Statutory 
reports by Regulated Entities to Reserve Bank of India (RBI)’ in Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 was 
recently amended through the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025.  
RBI draws its powers to regulate banks, Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) and All India 
Financial Institutions (AIFIs) from various statutes such as BR Act, RBI Act, FEMA Act, SARFAESI 
Act, etc. In some cases, activities of regulated entities may come within the purview of more than one 
regulator. Overlapping of regulatory powers of different regulators, if any, are being dealt through 
mutual consultations and by Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC)/ its Sub-
Committees, comprising all financial sector regulators which provide an institutional platform to 
resolve any inter-regulatory issues and to ensure consistency and clarity in policies.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4931 
ANSWERED ON- 23.03.2026 
 
Recruitment and Staff Position in University of Delhi 
 
†4931. Shri Murari Lal Meena: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the number of colleges presently affiliated and functioning under the University 
of Delhi along with the names, college-wise; 
(b) the total number of teaching and non -teaching staff presently working in the said un iversity 
and its affiliated colleges, post-wise and college-wise; 
(c) the number of recruitments made for various category of posts during the last five years, along 
with the details of appointments made in the Department of Law and the number of candidate s 
appointed therein, year -wise, category -wise, particularly with regard to Scheduled Caste (SC), 
Scheduled Tribe (ST) and Other Backward Class (OBC); 
(d) the total number of applications received and candidates selected in the recruitment made 
during the a bove said period along with the current status of vacancies, category -wise 
(General/SC/ST/OBC/EWS); and 
(e) the number of ST category posts advertised for recruitment in the year 2023 and 2024 and the 
number of ST candidates finally selected against those posts in the appointments made in the year 
2025? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to ( e): University of Delhi is statutory autonomous organization established under Delhi 
University Act, 1922 and is governed by provisions of the Statutes, Ordinances etc made 
thereunder. All administrative and academic decision are taken by the University with t he 
approval of its statutory bodies in accordance with statutory provisions and the relevant 
regulations/guidelines of the University Grants Commission (UGC). The details  of colleges 
functioning under the University of Delhi may be seen at the link https://www.du.ac.in. The 
University has informed that  87 Professors, 279 Associate Professor s, 734 Assistant Professors 
and 714 non-teaching employees are working in the Departments of the University. Further, 7603 
teaching and 2925 non-teaching employees are working in the colleges of the University. 
 
Occurrence and filling up of vacancies are continuous process . The onus to fill the vacant posts 
lies on the University. The vacancies arise due to retirement, resignation and additional 
requirements on account of enhanced students’ strength. Ministry of Education and University 
Grants Commission (UGC) regularly monitor the institutions for filling the vacant posts.  
 

From September 2022, all Central Universities have undertaken  recruitment drive in mission 
mode to fill the vacancies. Till 24.01.2026, more than 4040 teaching and non-teaching positions 
including 588 SC posts, 311 ST posts, 1070 OBC posts and 303 EWS posts have been filled in  
University of Delhi and its colleges . In last five years, 42 teaching staffs have been appointed in  
the Department of Law which include 5 SC, 10 OBC & 2 EWS.  
 
The UGC launched a unified recruitment portal i.e. CU -Chayan on 02.05.2023 to provide a 
common platform for listing of vacancies/ adve rtisements/ jobs across all Central Universities  for 
faculty posts. The Central Universities have also been instructed to publish rolling advertisements 
on their websites throughout the year to address the difficulties faced in getting eligible 
candidates. The Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Teachers Cadre) Act, 2019 has 
been notified on 09.07.2019 which provides for reservation of posts in direct recruitment for 
persons belonging to Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), Other Bac kward Classes 
(OBCs), and Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) in the Teacher’s Cadre of Central 
Educational Institutions established, maintained, or aided by the Central Government. This Act 
removes the difficulty regarding the reservation of posts in appoi ntment by treating 
University/Central Educational Institution as a unit for the purpose of reservation instead of 
individual departments. Further, by this Act from the year 2019, reservation was provided to 
Other Backward Class (OBC) in recruitment in Asso ciate Professor and Professor level. Earlier 
reservation to OBC was only in Assistant Professor level. Posts reserved for a particular category 
can only be filled by eligible persons of that particular category; any unfilled post belonging to 
any of the re served category will continue to be readvertised as backlog vacancies in that 
particular reserved category in next cycle(s) of recruitment, until filled.

wise, particularly in the States of West Bengal, Odisha and Damoh Lok Sabha Constituency of 
Madhya Pradesh; and the coverage of scholarships available on NSP for post-matric and higher 

education during the last three years  in Odisha, category-wise and district-wise  may be 
accessed at https://www.education.gov.in/parl_ques . 
To enhance awareness and outreach among students to improve access to various 
scholarship schemes available on NSP, the National Scholarship Portal (NSP) conducts open 
sessions wherein the NSP team provides guidance on registration, application submission, and 
verification procedures. N SP also actively responds to queries related to technical issues, 
process-related challenges, and policy -related clarifications. Further, to enhance accessibility 
of scholarships among rural and aspirational districts , the NSP is integrated with Common

ANSWERED ON 23/03/2026 
Lack of Internet Connectivity in Rural Schools 
 
4934. Shri Adhikari Deepak Dev:  
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
(a) whether the Government has assessed the lack of internet connectivity in schools in rural 
areas in the country, if so, the details thereof;  
(b) the total number and percentage at schools in rural areas that do not have internet 
connectivity;  
(c) whether the Government has assessed the impact on learning among students in 
Government schools in rural areas lacking internet connectivity; and  
(d) if so, the details of the reasons therefor? 
 
  
ANSWER   
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
(a) to (d) : Education is part of the Concurrent List of the Constitution and most of the 
Government schools are under the administration of the State Government and its bodies. The 
Ministry of Education imp lements ICT and Digital initiatives under Samagra Shiksha to 
enhance digital learning in Government schools across the country, including rural areas. 
At present, across India, 9,33,987 (63.5%) schools have internet connection. The State/UT 
wise list of rural schools with internet connection as per UDISE+ FY2024-25 report has been 
annexed. 
Availability of internet connectivity in the government schools in rural areas enables 
dissemination of digital content to teachers and students through Digital Infrastru cture for 
Knowledge Sharing (DIKSHA) It is the Nation’s digital infrastructure for providing quality 
e-content for school education in States/UTs and QR coded Energised Textbooks (ETBs) for 
all grades (One Nation, One Digital platform). It also helps the s tudents and teachers to get 
access to e-learning, teacher training, inclusive education, bridging the urban -rural education 
and latest technological interventions like AI. Reliable internet connectivity acts as the 
backbone for effective outreach of these digital programmes. 
The Government of India, in the Budget 2025, has announced provision of broadband 
connectivity to all Government Secondary schools in rural areas, under the ‘BharatNet’ 
project to enhance digital infrastructure in remote areas by BSNL in a phased manner.

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS;

and Protection Fund Authority under section 125(5) of the Companies 
Act, 2013. This Authority is entrusted with the responsibility of 
administration and utilisation of the Investor Educ ation and 
Protection Fund (IEPF) for making refunds of shares, unclaimed

awareness among investors, thereby protecting the interests of the 
investors.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCA TION AND LITERACY 
LOK SABHA

Children Covered under PM POSHAN Scheme in Andhra Pradesh 
 
4936. Shri P V Midhun Reddy: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the number of children covered under the PM POSHAN Scheme in Andhra Pradesh, district-
wise; 
 
(b) the details of availability of cook -cum-helpers, kitchen sheds and infrastructure in  
Government schools of the said State; 
 
(c) the details of food safety, nutrition quality and monitoring mechanisms in place; and 
 
(d) the details of special interventions for tribal, aspirational districts and remote areas of the said 
State? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (d):  Education is a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution of India and the majority 
of schools are under the administrative control of the respective State Government/Union Territory 
(UT) administration. Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman (PM POSHAN) Scheme is one of the 
foremost rights based Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented in partnership with the States and 
UTs for providing one hot cooked and nutritious meal to all children study ing in Bal Vatika (just 
before class-I) and classes I to VIII of Government and Government -aided schools.  The Scheme 
covers about 11 crore children in more than 10.35 lakh schools in all the States/UTs. The overall 
responsibility for smooth functioning of  the Scheme including providing hot cooked and nutritious 
meal to the eligible children as well as engagement of Cook-cum-Helpers (CCHs) lies with the 
States/UTs.  
 The district-wise number of children enrolled under the PM POSHAN Scheme as reported by 
State Government of Andhra Pradesh is at Annexure-I. Further, the State has also reported the details 
of CCHs, kitchen sheds and infrastructure in Andhra Pradesh which is at Annexure-II.  
The Government of India has issued detailed guidelines to improve the implementation of the 
scheme to all the States/UTs. These guidelines are available on official website 
https://pmposhan.education.gov.in . These guidelines, inter -alia, provide for instructions  to schools 
to procure Agmark quality and branded items for preparation of meals, training to CCHs, tasting of 

meals by members of School Management Committee including at least one teacher before serving 
the hot meal to children. The guidelines, inter-alia, provide for training of CCHs on nutrition, cooking 
processes, health and hygiene, preparation of raw grains and vegetables, recipes, serving skills etc. 
States/UTs are providing training to CCHs in collaboration with the Ministry of Tourism, 
Government of India through their Institutes of Hotel Management and Food Craft Institutes, FSSAI, 
State Agricultural Universities etc. States/ UTs are directed to conduct cooking competitions among 
CCHs to encourage them to cook varied and nutritious meals. Many States/ UTs are conducting the 
competitions and also giving cash prizes to the winners.  
The scheme also provides elaborate monitoring mechanism i.e. Empowered Committee under 
the Chairpersonship of the Hon’ble Union Education Minister, Programme Approval Board (PAB) 
under the Chairpersonship of the Secretary (DoSE&L), State Steering -cum-Monitoring Committee 
under the Chairpersonship of the Chief Secretary, District level Steering-cum- Monitoring Committee 
under the Chairpersonship of the District Collector. The PM Poshan Guidelines provides a District 
Level Committee under the Chairmanship of senior most Member of Parliament (MP) of the district 
to monitor the scheme on quarterly basis.  
There is a provision of 5% of total recurring budget as the flexi component to be used by the 
States/UTs for setting up of School Nutrition Gardens (SNGs) and provision of Supplementary 
Nutrition interventions in identified districts. Many States/UTs provide additional sup plementary 
nutrition interventions like egg, milk, chikki, fresh fruits, chicken, ragi malt etc.

†4937.   SMT. DIMPLE YADAV 
 
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to 
state?  
 
(a)  the details of availability of trades and actual enrolment figures related to food processing, 
cold-chain management and agro-logistics in Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) in Uttar Pradesh, 
particularly in Mainpuri district; 
 
(b)  the number of such trades that are non -functional due to vacant post of instructors or the 
lack of adequate faculties; 
 
(c)  the details of the placement record of youth trained in the said specialized fields within the 
agri-based processing industries; 
 
(d)  whether the Government has formulated a time -bound strategy to bridge the gap between 
local agricultural production and industrial requirements through targeted skill development 
initiatives; and 
 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL  
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a)      The Directorate General of Training (DGT), under the Ministry of Skill Development and 
Entrepreneurship (MSDE), implements the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) through a network 
of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) for skilling youth. Under CTS, trainin g is imparted in 169 
courses through 14,688 ITIs (3,345 Government and 11,343 Private) across the country. 
 
In the State of Uttar Pradesh, there are 3,304 ITIs, comprising 294 Government and 3,010 Private 
ITIs. Out of these, Mainpuri district has 21 ITIs, including 04 Government and 17 Private ITIs. 
 
In the areas related to food processing, cold -chain management and agro -logistics, Training is 
offered in 13 trades under CTS in ITIs across the country. The list of these 13 trades is available 
at Annexure-1. In the session 2025 –26, out of the se 13 trades , training in three trades  Food 
Beverage, Food Production (General), and Refrigeration and Air Conditioner Technician is offered 
in ITIs in the State of Uttar Pradesh with a total enrolment of 6,015 trainees. In Mainpuri district, in 
these sectors, training in Refrigeration and Air Conditioner Technician trade is offered in ITIs, with 
an enrolment of 120 trainees. 
 
(b)      The engagement of Instructors in Government ITIs falls under the jurisdiction of the 
respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations.  
 
(c) to (e)    The MSDE is also implementing the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 
for enhancing the employability of youth by equipping them with industry -relevant skills, including 
in sectors such as agriculture, food processing and cold-chain management. Under PMKVY, a total 
of 1,38,680 candidates have been trained/oriented in job-roles related to these sectors in the State 
of Uttar Pradesh up to 31.12.2025. In Mainpuri district, 317 candidates have been trained/oriented 
in these job-roles.

industrially backward districts are prioritised for upgradation under PM SETU, including districts in 
Karnataka along with the proposed timeline for completion; and 
 
(e)       the specific details of ITIs identified for upgradation in Bengaluru Urban and Bengaluru 
Rural districts? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP  
 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY)  
 
(a) to (d)         The Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability through Upgraded ITIs (PM -SETU) 
scheme envisages to enhance the overall quality and relevance of vocational training with 
upgraded labs, machines, and industry-aligned curriculum in the country. 
 
The key objectives of the scheme are: 
 
i. To improve the quality of training delivery in ITIs and NSTIs; 
ii. To modernize infrastructure and equipment as per industry standards; 
iii. To introduce industry-aligned long-term and short-term courses, especially in new and 
emerging sectors; 
iv. To strengthen industry linkage for demand-driven skilling and better employment 
outcomes; and 
v. To enhance the capacity of National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs) for training of trainers. 
 
The scheme comprises of two components: 
 
i. Component I – Upgradation of 1,000 Government ITIs (200 Hub ITIs and 800 Spoke ITIs) 
in a Hub and Spoke model wherein upgradation includes smart classrooms, modern labs, 
digital content, and new courses aligned to industry needs. 
ii. Component II – Capacity Augmentation of five NSTIs located in Bhubaneswar, Chennai, 
Hyderabad, Kanpur, and Ludhiana, including setting-up sector-specific National Centres of 
Excellence for skilling, with focus on advanced training of trainers with global partnership. 

PM-SETU is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with an outlay of ₹60,000 crore (Central Share: 
₹30,000 crore, State Share: ₹20,000 crore and Industry Share: ₹10,000 crore), with co -financing 
to the extent of 50% of Central share by the Asian Development Bank and the World Bank, 
equally. 
 
The selection of ITIs under PM -SETU scheme is led by the respective State/UT Governments in 
consultation with industry, ensuring alignment with emerging skill needs and local industrial 
potential. Accordingly, States/UTs are required to submit proposals for upgradation in 
collaboration with industry partners. Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) 
has constituted National Steering Committee (NSC) chaired by Secretary, MSDE, an apex body 
to provide the overall vision for the scheme, facilitate broad policy direction, finalize operational 
guidelines, monitor, and conduct course correction.   32 States/UTs have constituted their State 
Steering Committee (SSC) led by Chief Secretary of the State/UT, an apex body at the State/UT 
level for guiding and overseeing the implementation of scheme. 19 States/UTs have floated their 
proposal for inviting the interest of industry. For selection of the industry partner to form Special 
Purpose Vehicle (SPV), a Strategic Investment Plan (SIP) by industry is required to be submitted 
in response to the Request for Proposal (RFP).  
 
Progress under the scheme is monitored through Six (6) Disbursement Linked Indicators (DLIs), 
which are periodically reviewed through independent third -party verification. Indian Institute of 
Management Indore has been engaged to carry out this verification. 
 
The DLIs are as follows: 
 
I. DLI #1: Employment outcomes for graduates of supported ITIs improved. 
II. DLI #2: Access to better quality training programs of supported ITIs increased. 
III. DLI #3: Governance and management of supported ITIs strengthened. 
IV. DLI #4: State governance and leadership for enabling environment for ITI ecosystem 
strengthened. 
V. DLI #5: Quality of training at NSTIs increased. 
VI. DLI #6: National governance and leadership strengthened. 
  
(e)       The State Government of Karnataka has identified two clusters under the PM -SETU 
Scheme, with Hub ITIs located in the districts of Bengaluru and Kalaburagi. The State of 
Karnataka has floated Expression of Interest (EOI) for inviting industry proposal.  At present, no 
proposal or Strategic Investment Plan (SIP) from the State is pending for consideration or 
approval before the National Steering Committee (NSC). The details of the ITIs selected in

Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:  
(a) whether it is a fact that the States in the country have been demanding a larger share of devolution

(b) whether it is a fact that only 39 per cent gross tax revenue is shared with States as opposed to 41 per

Low Participation in Industrial Apprenticeship Training under NATS/NAPS in Tirupati 
 
4941. Shri Maddila Gurumoorthy: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
 
(a) the reasons for low industry participation in apprenticeship training under National 
Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS)/National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme 
(NAPS) in Tirupati district along with the steps proposed to be taken by the Government to 
incentivise more establishments to engage apprentices; 
(b) the status of awareness campaigns conducted to inform students and job seekers in the 
said district about apprenticeship opportunities under NATS/NAPS along with the measurable 
outcomes achieved from such initiatives; and 
(c) the specific measures taken by the Government to simplify compliance and administrative 
procedures for Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Tirupati to register and me ntor 
apprentices under the national apprenticeship framework? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
 
(a) to (c):  The Government is implementing apprenticeship training through the National 
Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) under Ministry of Skill Development and 
Entrepreneurship (MSDE) and the National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS)  under 
Ministry of Education (MoE), as per the provisions of the Apprentices Act, 1961. To facilitate 
greater participation, the Government has taken measures such as simplification of procedures 
through online portals, provision for centralized registration, enabli ng basic training by 
establishments and engagement of Third Party Aggregators to assist especially MSMEs in 
operational and compliance -related activities. Monitoring and review mechanisms have also 
been strengthened at multiple levels.  Currently 28 compani es from Tirupati are available 
under NATS.  
Workshops, stakeholder interactions and initiatives such as the Pradhan Mantri National 
Apprenticeship Mela (PMNAM) are conducted to promote apprenticeship training and 
facilitate effective coordination and engagement between industry, institutions and 
candidates. E stablishments in Andhra Pradesh, including Tirupati district, are participating 
under both schemes and candidates are being engaged through various outreach initiatives 
including PMNAM. 

The schemes provide for online processes relating to registration, contract generation, stipend 
payment and monitoring, thereby reducing procedural requirements for establishments, 
including MSMEs.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4943 
ANSWERED ON 23/03/2026 
 
INDIA SKILLS ACCELERATOR INITIATIVE 
 
†4943.  SHRI ASHOK KUMAR RAWAT: 
 
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT  AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)  the details of the current status of the India Skills Accelerator initiative launched in 
partnership with the World Economic Forum including information on participating stakeholders 
and its operational scope; 
 
(b)  the details of key objective and methodology of the said initiative to identify, scale and 
accelerate the implementation of innovative solutions for workforce upgradation and lifelong 
learning;  
 
(c)  the details of the number of skill development program mes, enrolled learners and 
industry partnerships under the said initiative to reduce the skills gap across all sectors; 
 
(d)  whether the Government proposes any impact assessment or performance framework to 
evaluate the outcomes of the said initiative; and  
 
(e)  if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a to c)      The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) has partnered with 
the World Economic Forum (WEF) for the India Skill Accelerator initiative, and a Memorandum 
of Understanding (MoU) was signed  in 2026 for cooperation in the fields of Skill Development 
and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET). 
 
Under the MoU,  the India Skill Accelerator is envisaged as a multi -stakeholder platform to 
facilitate identification, scaling and acceleration of innovative solutions and public –private 
partnerships to address skill gaps and strengthen the TVET ecosystem in the country. The 
initiative involves participation from Government, industry, academia, training providers and 
other relevant stakeholders. 
 
The initiative envisages alignment of skill training and reskilling with industry requirements, 
promotion of innovative financing mechanisms, and enhanced coordination among stakeholders 
in line with India’s Vision @2047. It also provides for alignment with the National Education 
Policy 2020 through flexible learning pathways and use of frameworks such as the Academic 
Bank of Credits, while leveraging Higher Educational Institutions (HEIs) and regulatory bodies 
such as All India Council for Technical Education and University Grants Commission. 
 
Further, the initiative focuses on emerging global skill demand trends, facilitation of mobility 
through mutual recognition of qualifications, promotion of innovation activities, and engagement 
in “Future of Work” domains and entrepreneurship. 

The initiative is presently in the initial phase of operationalizatioin and is focused on establishing 
the institutional and partnership framework for implementation. Accordingly, specific skill 
development programmes, learner enrollment and industry partnership figures under this 
initiative will evolve as the Action plan and pilot interventions are operationalized. 
 
(d) & (e)      The monitoring and implementation framework has been envisaged under the MoU. 
It includes participation of Government and private sector stakeholders and preparation of an 
Action Plan outlining the roles and responsibilities of stakeholders. MSDE, through its agencies, 
will oversee implementation of agreed upon project milestones and outputs, and monitor 
progress of the initiative through periodic review mechanisms.

Extension of Implementation of NIPUN Bharat Scheme 
 
4948. Shri Naveen Jindal: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of changes made in schools teaching pattern to implement National Initiative for 
Proficiency in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy (NIPUN) Bharat format of teaching 
in the country; 
 
(b) the extent of implementation of NIPUN Bharat scheme across the country; and 
 
(c) the details of progress made so far in regard to implementation of NIPUN Bharat initiative 
in terms of achieving the initiative's goals and objectives? 
 
ANSWER 
 
 MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
 (SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
(a) to (c): The Department of School Education & Literacy (DoSE&L), Ministry of 
Education (MoE) has launched a National Mission called “National Initiative for Proficiency 
in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy (NIPUN Bharat Mission (NBM)) ” on 5th July, 
2021 for ensuring that every child in the country necessarily attains foundational literacy and 
numeracy (FLN) by the end of Grade 2. This Mission aligned with the National Educatio n 
Policy (NEP) 2020, has been set up under the aegis of the centrally sponsored scheme of 
Samagra Shiksha- an integrated scheme for School Education. Under Samagra Shiksha, all 36 
States/Union Territories are implementing the NBM.  Under the NBM, a range of  systemic 
interventions have been undertaken and the following progress has been made across the 
country: 
 
(i) A 3-months play based ‘School Preparation Module and Guidelines ’ for Grade I named 
‘Vidya Pravesh’ was launched on 29th July, 2021. The goal of Vidya Pravesh programme is to 
promote school preparedness in all children coming to Grade -I from diverse backgrounds 
(Balvatika, Anganwadi Centers (AWCs), at home, private play schools etc.), to ensure a smooth 
transition of children to Grade-I. It provides play based, age and developmentally appropriate 

learning experiences in a joyful and stimulating environment leading to holistic development 
to bolster a child ’s pre-literacy, pre-numeracy, cognitive and social skills. This programme is 
being implemented across the country. From 2022-23 till date, over 4.2 crore students in around 
8.9 lakh schools have benefitted. The Vidya Pravesh Programme is a new initiative so that the 
children are school ready.    
 
(ii) To improve the learning outcomes at foundational  stage, the National Curricular 
Framework for Foundational Stage (NCF-FS) was released on 20th October, 2022 providing a 
structure for the syllabus, training of teachers, Learning Teaching Material (LTM), etc.  The 
NEP, 2020 recommends a toy based pedagogy for FLN for joyful learning. The various LTMs 
being used for the same are as under: 
 
• The Jaadui Pitara (JP), a set of 53 play-based learning-teaching materials for ages 3-8 
was launched on 20th February 2023. Available in 22 Indian languages, JP includes toys, 
puzzles, story cards, flashcards, and teacher handbooks. Its digital extension, the e-
Jaadui Pitara, launched on 10 th February 2024, offers multilingual stories, activities, 
songs in 22 Indian languages, and AI-based bots-Katha Sakhi, Teacher Tara, and Parent 
Tara-to support children, teachers, and parents. As envisaged in NEP 2020, these 
initiatives are an integral part of the foundational stage. 
 
• Primers (launched in March, 2024) have bee n developed in 121 local and tribal 
languages for FLN in mother tongues spoken by populations of at least 10,000.  
 
(iii) Lakshyas or Targets for FLN starting from the Balvatika -3 upto Grade -2, based on the 
learning outcomes have been developed on the basis of national and international research.  
 
(iv) The Government of India conducts periodic large -scale assessments, to measure learning 
and education outcomes across the country, through PARAKH (Performance Assessment, 
Review, and Analysis of Knowledge for Holistic Development) Rashtriya Sarvekshan, which 
is conducted by National Assessment Centre, PARAKH under the aegis of the Ministry of 
Education. The primary objective of this survey is to evaluate the learning competencies of 
students at the end of each  of the educational stages i.e. Foundational, Preparatory, and 
Middle. The latest PARAKH Rashtriya Sarvekshan was conducted on December 4, 2024. A 
comparative analysis of State -wise average scores at foundational stage during National 
Achievement Survey  (NAS) 2021 and PRS 2024 reflects the depth and impact of NIPUN 
Bharat Mission. There is an improvement in learning achievements of the students in Grade 3 
survey results, respectively reflecting the success of NIPUN Bharat Mission across the country. 
It also shows that the performance of children in Grade 3 in rural and government schools is 

better than urban and private schools, indicating clear improvement in learning outcomes from 
previous survey. This can be accessed at https://dashboard.parakh.ncert.gov.in/en.   
 
The Department of School Education & Literacy ( DoSE&L) has launched a national 
initiative to improve learning outcomes through an integrated teacher training programme 
called the National Initiative for School Heads ’ and Teachers ’ Holistic Advancement 
(NISHTHA) under Samagra Shiksha. NISHTHA supports large -scale in -service teacher 
capacity building and includes training modules for primary teachers focusing on pedagogy, 
FLN, inclusive education and classroom practices, and is implemented in coordination with the 
States and Union Territories through face-to-face and online modes. More than 15.57 lakh users 
including pre -primary teachers, master trainers and Anganwadi Workers have completed 
NISHTHA online training program for FLN & ECCE. Besides, these states are also conducting 
physical trainings of teachers at State level. 
 Further, Government has introduced the Integrated Teacher Education Programme 
(ITEP), regulated by the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE), in order to improve 
the quality of teachers, especially for young children at the foundational stage. It is a four-year 
integrated course that prepares future teachers in a comprehensive way. It combines studies on 
child development, early childhood care and education (ECCE), and modern teaching methods 
like play-based and activity-based learning. It focuses on Foundational Literacy and Numeracy 
(FLN), which are essential skills for early education.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-4949 
ANSWERED ON-23/03/2026 
 
Implementation of Mother-Tongue Based Education 
 
4949. Adv Gowaal Kagada Padavi: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the National Education Policy (NEP) and subsequent policy decisions have 
provision for teaching in local and tribal languages at foundational and primary levels to 
improve comprehension among students, particular ly in tribal districts such as Nandurbar in 
Maharashtra, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) the details of specific steps taken by the Government to develop curriculum, textbooks and 
digital learning content in tribal languages and dialects, including collaboration with linguistic 
experts and State authorities; 
 
(c) whether teachers are being recruited or trained with multilingual competencies to 
implement mother-tongue-based education effectively; 
 
(d) the details of the financial and institutional support e xtended to States for promoting 
regional language instruction in schools; and 
 
(e) the measurable Impact of these initiatives on learning outcomes, enrolment and retention 
among tribal students? 
 
ANSWER 
 
 MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
 (SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
(a) to (e):  The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 recognizes the vital role of 
multilingualism and mother tongue based education . Para 4.12 of NEP 2020 emphasizes that 
wherever possible, the medium of instruction until at least Grade 5, and preferably till Grade 8 
and beyond, should be the child ’s mother tongue/home language/local language. This is 
reinforced by the National Curriculum Framework for School Education (NCFSE) 2023, which 
places the child ’s linguistic context at th e heart of learning and lays a clear roadmap for 

structured multilingual education and the following initiatives have been taken in the area of 
school education to promote Indian languages:   
 (i) NCERT has developed and published textbooks in 22 scheduled  languages for 
Grades 1 to 3 and 6.  Similarly, all books of classes 4,5,7 to 12 will be published in all Schedule 
8 languages and English. The textbooks are available at NCERT’s website https://ncert.nic.in. 
 (ii) The Jaadui Pitara (JP), a set of 53 play -based learning-teaching materials for 
ages 3-8 was launched on 20 th February 2023. Available in 22 Indian languages and English, 
JP includes toys, puzzles, story cards, flashcards, and teacher handbooks. Its digital extension, 
the e-Jaadui Pitara, launched on 10th February 2024, offers multilingual stories, activities, songs 
in 22 Indian languages. As envisaged in NEP 2020, these initiatives are an integral part of the 
foundational stage. 
 (iii) The Ministry of Education  (MoE) through NCERT and Central Institute of 
Indian Languages (CIIL), Mysuru along with the Tribal Institutes has developed Primers  
(launched in March, 2024) in 121 local languages including tribal lanaguage for FLN in mother 
tongues spoken by populations  of at least 10,000. Primers are available at 
https://ncert.nic.in/primers.php?ln=en.   
 (iv) The Ministry of Education initiated a nationwide programme to promote all 
Indian languages through the prog ramme of Bhasha Sangam. Children in school learn 100 
sentences in the 22 scheduled languages with audio and video support. Schools across the 
country are participating and learning the Indian languages. Both textual and audio -video 
materials are available on DIKSHA portal at https://ncert.nic.in/bs-2021.php.  
 (v) The Rashtriya e-Pustakalaya provides quality books to children and adolescents, 
ensuring accessibility across diverse geographies, languages, genre s, and education al levels. 
The platform offers 6 ,000+ non -academic books in 23 languages making a wide range of 
resources available to users. 
 (vi) The PM e-Vidya initiative has expanded to 200 DTH TV channels with vision 
of “One Nation, One Digital Platfo rm”, delivering curriculum-aligned content in various 128 
Indian languages and 7 foreign languages, enhancing reach and inclusivity of rural area. 
 (vii) Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has prescribed using child ’s 
home language, mother tongue or a familiar regional language , as a medium of instruction at 
the foundational stage and also at the preparatory stage. The notification dated 
22.05.2025 is available at https://cbseacademic.nic.in/web_material/Circulars/2025/30_Circul
ar_2025.pdf 
 

The Department of School Education and Literacy has also launched a National 
Mission to improve learning outcomes at the elementary level through an Integrated Teacher 
Training Programme called NISHTHA – National Initiative for School Heads ’ and Teachers’ 
Holistic Advancement under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Samagra Shiksha in 2019-20. 
Under NISHTHA FLN, modules such as ‘Multilingual Education in Primary Grades ’ are 
specifically included to equip teachers with strategies for addressing linguistic diversity in 
classrooms. 
The National Professional Standards for Teachers (NPST), developed by NCTE under 
para 5.20 of NEP 2020, establishes a uniform framework for teacher competency. To facilitate 
this, NPST guiding document was released by NCTE, available in accessible formats including 
Braille, audio, and 22 scheduled languages. It guides teachers to create inclusive learning 
environments that respect and integrate students ’ home languages, thereby strengthening 
multilingual education in classrooms and supporting equitable lear ning outcomes across 
diverse linguistic contexts. 
The Four -Year Integrated Teacher Education Programme (ITEP), aligned with the 
National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, is designed to prepare professionally competent 
teachers through a multidisciplinary and h olistic approach that integrates content, pedagogy, 
values, and practice. The programme emphasizes grounding student -teachers in Indian 
languages, cultural contexts, and Indian knowledge systems, including tribal traditions, while 
equipping them with skills to address diverse classroom realities.  
States/UTs including Maha rashtra are encouraged through review meetings, PAB 
meetings and other platforms to operationalize multilingual strategies by mapping learners ’ 
mother tongues, facilitating availability of  learning materials in local languages, and training 
teachers for multilingual pedagogies. 
 
Financial assistance is provided to States and UTs (including Maharashtra) for 
implementation of the interventions under Samagra Shiksha (including promotion of regional 
languages instructions in schools)  as per the Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWP&B) under 
Samagra Shiksha prepared by the States and UTs based on their requirements and priority.  
 
The Government of India conducts periodic large -scale assessments, t o measure 
learning and education outcomes across the country , through PARAKH  (Performance 
Assessment, Review, and Analysis of Knowledge for Holistic Development)  Rashtriya 

Sarvekshan, which is conducted by National Assessment Centre, PARAKH under the aegis of 
the Ministry of Education . The primary objective of this survey is to evaluate the learning 
competencies of students at the end of each of the educational stages i.e. Foundational, 
Preparatory, and Middle . The latest PARAKH Rashtriya Sarvekshan  was conducted on 
December 4, 2024. A comparative analysis of State-wise average scores at foundational stage 
during National Achievement Survey (NAS) 2021 and PRS 2024 reflects the depth and impact 
of NIPUN Bharat Mission. 
 There is an improvement in learning achievements of the students reflecting the success 
of NIPUN Bharat Mission across the country. It also shows that the performance of children in 
Grade 3 in rural and government schools is better than urban and private s chools, indicating 
clear improvement in learning outcomes from previous survey. This can be accessed at 
https://dashboard.parakh.ncert.gov.in/en.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 4950 
ANSWERED ON 23/03/2026 
 
UGC Grants for Colleges in Bargarh and Jharsuguda Districts 
 
4950. Shri Pradeep Purohit: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the University Grants Commission (UGC) has sanctioned any grants to Government 
colleges in the districts of Bargarh and Jharsuguda during the last three years; 
 
(b) if so, the details of the grants sanctioned, released and the amount utilised by each college 
during the said period, district-wise and college-wise; 
 
(c) whether any proposals from Government colleges of Bargarh and Jharsuguda districts are 
pending with the UGC for financial assistance, if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to ensure timely release and effective utilisation of UGC 
grants for strengthening higher education infrastructure in these said two districts? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (d): The University Grants Commission (UGC)  has informed that no grants have been 
sanctioned/released to Government colleges in the districts of Bargarh and Jharsuguda during 
the last three years.  The funding under UGC schemes is released under specific schemes of 
the UGC, and presently, there is no active/open call for grants-in-aid proposals from UGC.  
Further, Ministry of Education is implementing Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan 
(RUSA) which is a  Centrally Sponsored Scheme aimed at funding specific State government 
universities and colleges, so as to improve their quality by ensuring their conformity to prescribed 
norms and standards. In alignment with National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, the Government 
has launched the third phase of Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA) in June 2023 in 
the form of Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM -USHA) for the period 2023 -24 to 
2025-26 with an outlay of Rs. 12926.10 crore, to cater to the needs of educationally unserved/ 
underserved areas. The scheme has been further extended till 31st March,2028, for completion 
of PM-USHA projects and for an additional 6 months (i.e.,30th September, 2026) for completion 
of ongoing RUSA projects. 
Under this scheme, 199 projects with a total approved amount of Rs. 1581.66 crore have 
been approved for the state of Odisha including 6 units amounting to Rs. 15  crore in Bargarh 
district and 5 units amounting to Rs. 12.99 crore in Jharsuguda district.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
  
LOK SABHA
